Reseller demand arrives in monthly batches, not as a steady
All reseller revenue lands on ~1 batch date per month,
so month-over-month swings are scheduling, not demand.

Every Mountain-100 variant contributes $5.2k–$5.7k per order — the line is what matters,
Net revenue of the product ÷ orders containing it · minimum 30 orders · net, because question b defines the measure after
Axis starts at $5,100, not zero — the spread is under 9%, so a zero-based bar chart would show six identical bars.

Complete product lines by gross sales · every variant included
Per variant, Road-250 averages $1.73M against Mountain-200's $3.72M —
the gap is the line's pull, not the number of sizes carried.

Who buys, how concentrated the revenue is, and where it ships
of gross sales · no account is critical
Concentrated by segment, not by account — the distinction changes what to protect
The top 10% of customers (~1,900 resellers) hold 81.7% of gross sales, yet the largest single account is 0.8%. The risk to
manage is losing the reseller channel, not losing a customer.
No single customer exceeds 0.8% of gross sales — the ten largest together hold just 7.2%
Together they hold only 7.2% of gross sales — losing any one of them is survivable.
Toronto alone is 4.1% of global gross sales —
more than Germany, an entire country, at 4.5%.
Gross sales by country · share of total
but only 125 reseller orders — a pure online market
Canada is the mirror image: resellers are 88%
Customer counts come from the fact table. dim_customer holds 19,820 rows but ~19,185 real customers: each of the 635 selling resellers has an inactive twin record under the same store_id.

Online channel only — resellers never record a sales reason
Every widget on this page is filtered to online orders (27,659 orders · $29.4M gross). All 3,806 reseller orders are structurally incapable of carrying a sales reason.
Promotions are recorded only on bike orders — never on an accessory-only basket
Which is why promotion performance must be judged against other bike orders, not against all orders
Price is the leading declared reason; three marketing channels have never produced an
Online orders citing each sales reason
Slate bars are absences, not reasons. An order can cite up to 3 reasons, so this column cannot be totalled.
Controlled for product mix, promotion orders are worth 5% LESS than comparable bike orders
Average order value of online orders · bike orders isolated
Against ALL other online orders this would read +90% — that is bikes vs. bottles, not the promotion.
No online order line carries a discount: the ‘On Promotion’ reason is not linked to any recorded price benefit, so promotion ROI cannot be measured today.

Any dimension, the same three measures — the table every other page's numbers come from
Group the detail table by any dimension
The grouping below drives the table; every global filter applies
Orders, quantity purchased and total transaction value — grouped by product
Showing the top 9 of 266 products sold · 31,465 orders · 274,914 units · $110,373,889 with no filter applied

ORDERS counts orders CONTAINING the row's item, so it is non-additive under Product, Sales reason, City and Customer — only Order month and Status partition orders cleanly. GROSS / ORDER is the item's own contribution, not the value of the whole order. Grouping by sales
reason also switches the base to online only (27,659 orders · $29.4M), since resellers never record one.
Each action is carried by a page above, and each names the number that justifies it
2nd-highest order count, only 125 reseller orders — p.3
Stop crediting promotions with a +90% lift
controlled for bikes they run 5% BELOW comparable orders — p.4
Tie every promotion to a discount code
today 0% of promotion lines carry one, so ROI is unmeasurable — p.4
